name.local: SPARK Taiwan 生醫轉譯加速器

strategy.thesis: Government-backed biomedical translational-research accelerator modeled on Stanford SPARK, supervised by Taiwan's National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) and executed by the Science & Technology Policy Research and Information Center (STPI) of NARL; runs through partner university/hospital nodes to translate academic biomedical research into investable startups.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Operates through anchor academic/medical institutions including National Taiwan University, Taipei Medical University, Fu Jen Catholic University, Chang Gung University, China Medical University, National Cheng Kung University, and Kaohsiung Medical University, each running its own SPARK-affiliated translational program (e.g. NTU SPARK).

perks: translational bootcamps and commercialization workshops
mentorship and networking with industry/VC
annual SPARK Asia Showcase and Global Conference exposure
connections to Silicon Valley resources

strategy.thesis: One of Taiwan's longest-running dedicated biotech incubators, located in Nangang Software Park adjacent to the Biotechnology Development Center (DCB), Academia Sinica, and major teaching hospitals; provides wet-lab-adjacent facilities and shared R&D equipment to grow biotech, biomedical and healthcare-services companies toward listing.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Co-located with and managed by the Biotechnology Development Center (DCB, 生物技術開發中心) since January 2017; leverages DCB's R&D database and shared precision instruments.

perks: on-site shared R&D equipment and precision instruments
access to DCB's technical/electronic library
dedicated in-house incubation managers for project mentoring

track_record.portfolio_count: 66 companies incubated cumulatively since 2004; 47 graduated; 6 have listed on stock exchanges

name.en: NHRI Technology Transfer & Innovation Incubation Center (TTIC)
name.local: 國家衛生研究院技轉及育成中心

strategy.thesis: Wet-lab and office incubation arm of Taiwan's National Health Research Institutes (NHRI), providing bench space and technology-transfer support to companies and individuals developing biotechnology, drug-development, biomedical-engineering, and healthcare products, with priority given to NHRI licensees/collaborators.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Located within NHRI's Zhunan, Miaoli campus; resident companies include biosimilar, influenza-vaccine, drug-development-services, and antibody-research firms.

perks: wet-lab and office space at fixed per-square-foot rent
'virtual stationing' option for companies not needing physical presence
technology transfer / IP support from NHRI

application.eligibility: Registered Taiwan companies developing life-science products/services, individual entrepreneurs with proprietary biomedical technology, or organizations with NHRI licensing/cooperation agreements (priority).

sources.title: 育成進駐 – 【國家衛生研究院】技轉及育成中心
sources.supports: location, lab/office rent structure, eligibility, resident company sectors
sources.quote: The center provides laboratory and office facilities at NT$1,200 per square foot monthly, plus utility costs (NT$500/sq ft for labs, NT$105/sq ft for offices). A 'virtual stationing plan' offers an alternative at NT$30,000 annually for companies not requiring physical presence.

verification_notes: Directly fetched from NHRI's own ttic.nhri.edu.tw domain, a government research institute (national institutes of health equivalent), making this a primary source. Founding year and total portfolio count not stated on the page fetched.

name.local: 國家生技研究園區創服育成中心
